questions.scenario: A huge fight breaks out in the school corridor between two senior sections over a cricket match. What is your reaction?

options.A: Jump right in the middle, physically separate the two angriest guys, and stop the punches from flying.
options.B: Stand back and observe exactly who threw the first punch and what triggered the actual fight.
options.C: Quickly block the staircase and direct the younger kids away so they don't get caught in the stampede.
options.D: Take total charge, shout a loud command to freeze, and threaten to take the leaders straight to the Principal's office.

questions.scenario: You are watching an intense episode of 'CID' or 'Crime Patrol' with your family after dinner. What are you doing?

options.A: Cheering the loudest when Daya breaks the door down or when the cops chase the criminal through a narrow gully.
options.B: Guessing the murderer in the first 10 minutes by noticing a small clue that even the TV detectives missed.
options.C: Pointing out the flaws in the layout of the crime scene and explaining how the criminal could have easily escaped out the back.
options.D: Judging how the senior inspector interrogates the suspects and manages his team of junior officers.

questions.scenario: You are put in charge of the main entry gate during the massive annual school fest. How do you handle it?

options.A: Personally chasing down and throwing out kids from rival schools who are trying to sneak in by jumping the boundary wall.
options.B: Carefully inspecting every single pass and catching the forged stamps or fake ID cards that other volunteers missed.
options.C: Rearranging the barricades and entry lines to ensure the huge crowd moves smoothly without any pushing or stampede.
options.D: Delegating tasks to your juniors, taking walkie-talkie updates, and confidently handling angry parents at the VIP gate.

questions.scenario: Someone keeps stealing the tastiest items from your best friend's tiffin box during the PT period. How do you solve this?

options.A: Hiding behind the classroom door during the PT period to jump out and catch the tiffin chor red-handed.
options.B: Checking the desk for oily fingerprints and analyzing who in the class suddenly smells like paneer paratha.
options.C: Finding a brilliant hidden spot in the classroom or changing the bag's placement so the thief can't reach it.
options.D: Making an official announcement in class that if the stealing doesn't stop today, you will report it to the class teacher.

questions.scenario: The teacher is 10 minutes late, and the class is screaming at the top of their lungs. As the Class Monitor, you...

options.A: Bang the duster on the desk aggressively and shout louder than everyone else to establish immediate, pin-drop silence.
options.B: Quietly note down the names of the main culprits on the blackboard to show the teacher exactly who started the chaos.
options.C: Stand strategically near the door to keep watch and signal the class the exact second the teacher is spotted down the hall.
options.D: Take control of the podium, calm everyone down, and smoothly engage them in a quiet game of Atlas or Dumb Charades.

questions.scenario: A notorious senior on the school bus is constantly bullying a junior kid. What is your move?

options.A: Confronting the senior directly, standing between them, and physically shielding the junior from being pushed.
options.B: Quietly observing the senior's daily routine to gather solid 'proof' of the bullying to hand over to the bus conductor.
options.C: Switching your seat strategically to sit next to the junior every single day so the senior simply cannot approach them.
options.D: Speaking to the bus uncle and organizing a permanent change in the seating arrangement to keep all juniors safe.

questions.scenario: A local celebrity is arriving as the Chief Guest for the Annual Day, and the crowd is going crazy. Your role?

options.A: Volunteering to be the tough 'bodyguard' who walks right next to the Chief Guest, physically clearing the path.
options.B: Doing a deep background check on the guest online to know exactly what controversies they might be questioned about.
options.C: Planning the exact walking route from the parking lot to the stage so they don't get mobbed by excited selfie-seekers.
options.D: Taking the role of the Head Coordinator, shaking hands with the guest, and guiding the whole school program flawlessly.

questions.scenario: A rumor spreads that the Maths pre-board question paper has leaked on a secret WhatsApp group. What do you do?

options.A: Demand the phone from the kid showing it off and instantly delete the forward to stop the immediate spread.
options.B: Trace the forwarded message back through multiple friends to find out who the original 'leaker' actually was.
options.C: Advise your close friend group to stay completely away from this specific group to avoid getting caught in the crossfire.
options.D: Calmly inform the subject teacher privately so they can change the paper before the exam, saving the school's reputation.

questions.scenario: A highly aggressive stray dog suddenly enters the school playground while junior kids are playing. You...

options.A: Grab a sports stick and bravely stand in front of the younger kids to scare the dog away from them.
options.B: Observe the dog's behavior closely to see if it's actually dangerous or just hungry and looking for canteen scraps.
options.C: Direct all the kids to quickly climb onto the jungle gym while keeping the main exit gate clear for the dog to leave.
options.D: Quickly call the school guards, instruct them on how to handle it safely, and keep the panicking students calm.

questions.scenario: The discipline committee is doing a surprise bag checking for mobile phones. How do you participate?

options.A: Taking the lead in actively and thoroughly searching every pocket and hidden zipper of the most suspicious students.
options.B: Catching the overly smart kids who hid their phones inside hollowed-out geometry boxes or inside their socks.
options.C: Noticing exactly how kids are trying to pass their phones out the window and sealing off those escape routes.
options.D: Managing the entire checking operation, dealing with the arguments, and deciding what the final punishment should be.

Role_1.title: Field Commando / Encounter Specialist
Role_1.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate action hero! You are brave, physically active, and never back down from a direct confrontation. When danger arrives, you are the first one to step up and shield others.
Role_1.day_in_the_life: Leading high-risk operations, raiding criminal hideouts, performing hostage rescues, and dealing with live threats on the ground with elite physical fitness and weapon training.
Role_1.alternative_match_text: Your bravery and physical readiness also make you a fantastic fit for the Indian Army, Fire & Rescue Services, or specialized Disaster Response Forces.
Role_1.educational_roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th works! After 12th, you can target the NDA exam. After graduation, clear the UPSC CAPF exam to become an Assistant Commandant in forces like CRPF or BSF, or clear State Police exams to join elite anti-terror squads like ATS or NSG (Black Cats) via deputation.

Role_2.title: Crime Branch / Forensics Inspector
Role_2.primary_match_text: You are the sharp-eyed detective! You have a brilliant analytical mind, and nothing escapes your observation. You love solving puzzles, connecting the dots, and finding the hidden truth.
Role_2.day_in_the_life: Arriving at complex crime scenes, dusting for fingerprints, analyzing digital footprints, interrogating suspects to catch their lies, and solving mysteries that stump regular cops.
Role_2.alternative_match_text: Your investigative mindset is also perfect for careers in Cybersecurity, Private Investigation, Intelligence Bureau (IB), or Data Analytics.
Role_2.educational_roadmap: Take Science (PCM/PCB) in 11th/12th if you want hardcore Forensics (B.Sc Forensic Science). If you prefer the detective police route, any stream works! Pursue graduation, then clear the SSC CGL exam to become a Sub-Inspector in CBI, or clear State PSC exams for CID roles.

Role_3.title: VIP Security / Crowd Strategist
Role_3.primary_match_text: You are the master protector! You have a highly spatial and creative mind. You can scan a room, spot the vulnerabilities, and design foolproof systems to keep people completely safe.
Role_3.day_in_the_life: Designing security formations for the Prime Minister or celebrities, analyzing building blueprints for escape routes, and managing massive crowds during Kumbh Mela or huge concerts.
Role_3.alternative_match_text: Your strategic and spatial planning skills make you an excellent fit for Event Management, Urban Planning, or Corporate Risk Management.
Role_3.educational_roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th. Complete your graduation and clear the UPSC CAPF exam. Choose CISF (Central Industrial Security Force) which handles VIP and Airport security, or aim for the elite SPG (Special Protection Group) via deputation from the police forces.

Role_4.title: Station House Officer (SHO) / Commissioner
Role_4.primary_match_text: You are the natural-born leader! You know how to take charge of chaotic situations, manage people, and make the tough decisions. You command respect and know how to run the system.
Role_4.day_in_the_life: Running an entire police district, addressing the media during high-profile cases, assigning duties to hundreds of officers, and maintaining law and order in the city.
Role_4.alternative_match_text: Your supreme leadership and PR skills translate perfectly into Civil Administration (IAS), Corporate Management, Politics, or Public Relations.
Role_4.educational_roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th. Get a strong undergraduate degree. To reach the absolute top, clear the UPSC Civil Services Examination (CSE) and choose the IPS (Indian Police Service). Alternatively, clear State PSC exams to become a DySP, or SSC CPO to become a Sub-Inspector and rise to SHO.
